name: theme
title: Theme
author: Pluto Systems <https://plutosystems.co>
description: The light and dark switch: a head script that sets the theme before paint, a store that follows the system until a choice is made, and a toggle button.

files.content:
<script lang="ts" module>
  /**
   * The head script, as a constant (005 decision 6). It reads the key
   * `theme.svelte.ts` writes, else the system's preference, and sets the
   * `dark` class before first paint. Storage may be unavailable. The key is
   * written here and in `theme.svelte.ts`; the two must agree.
   */
  export const THEME_SCRIPT = [
    "(function () {",
    '  var query = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";',
    "  var dark;",
    "  try {",
    '    var stored = localStorage.getItem("pluto-theme");',
    '    dark = stored ? stored === "dark" : matchMedia(query).matches;',
    "  } catch (e) {",
    "    dark = matchMedia(query).matches;",
    "  }",
    '  document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", dark);',
    "})();",
  ].join("\n");
</script>

<script lang="ts">
  let {
    nonce,
  }: {
    /** For an app with a Content Security Policy: SvelteKit's own nonces never reach a script written through `{@html}`. */
    nonce?: string;
  } = $props();

  // A nonce is base64; anything else is dropped rather than written into markup.
  const attribute = $derived(
    nonce ? ` nonce="${nonce.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]/g, "")}"` : "",
  );
  const tag = $derived(`<script${attribute}>${THEME_SCRIPT}</${"script"}>`);
</script>

<!--
  Rendered once, in the app's root layout, so the script is in the
  server-rendered head, which prerendering keeps. An item cannot edit an app's
  app.html; this is the same route mode-watcher takes. The string is a
  constant, not input.
-->
<svelte:head>
  {@html tag}
</svelte:head>

<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import Moon from "phosphor-svelte/lib/Moon";
  import Sun from "phosphor-svelte/lib/Sun";
  import { Button, type ButtonProps } from "$UI$/button";
  import { theme } from "./theme.svelte.js";

  let {
    size = "icon",
    ...restProps
  }: Omit<ButtonProps, "size" | "children" | "href"> & {
    /** 48 px (`icon`, the default) or 32 px (`icon-sm`). */
    size?: "icon" | "icon-sm";
  } = $props();

  // Until hydration the server markup cannot know the theme the head script
  // chose, so the button states no pressed value rather than a wrong one, and
  // shows the light icon. `data-ready` marks the moment for tests.
  let ready = $state(false);
  onMount(() => {
    ready = true;
  });
  const dark = $derived(ready && theme.resolved === "dark");
</script>

<!--
  One control, one state: a pressed button named "Dark theme", pressed when
  dark is in force. A tri-state choice (light, dark, system) is an app's to
  compose from dropdown-menu and theme.set; the item page shows it.
-->
<Button
  variant="ghost"
  {size}
  data-slot="theme-toggle"
  aria-label="Dark theme"
  aria-pressed={ready ? dark : undefined}
  data-ready={ready ? "" : undefined}
  onclick={() => theme.toggle()}
  {...restProps}
>
  {#if dark}
    <Moon aria-hidden="true" />
  {:else}
    <Sun aria-hidden="true" />
  {/if}
</Button>
